class.name: NetwBitBufferWriter
class.brief_description: Bit-granular writer used by [NetwCodec] to pack quantized values without byte rounding.
class.description: A quantized field occupies exactly its declared width. The writer accumulates bits LSB-first and flushes whole bytes, and [NetwBitBufferReader] serves them back in the same order. Byte-aligned helpers exist for framing headers and the raw [method @GlobalScope.var_to_bytes] fallback, so a packet mixes a byte-aligned header, a bit-packed payload, and an aligned tail coherently. Writing and reading are separate types because they are separate roles. One object holding both would carry a single bit accumulator for two cursors, so handing the same instance to an encode and a decode path would corrupt both silently. [codeblock] var w := NetwBitBufferWriter.new() w.put_aligned_u32(tick) # header, byte-aligned w.put_bits(quantized_x, 11) # payload, bit-packed w.put_bits(quantized_y, 11) var bytes := w.to_bytes() # flushes the partial final byte [/codeblock] Widths come from the shared synchronizer config on both peers, never the wire, so a one-bit offset cannot drift between encoder and decoder.

method.name: align
method.description: Flushes any partial byte (zero-padded) so the next write is byte-aligned.

method.name: put_aligned_u16
method.description: Aligns, then writes a 16-bit little-endian value.

method.name: put_aligned_u32
method.description: Aligns, then writes a 32-bit little-endian value.

method.name: put_bits
method.description: Writes the low [param count] bits of [param value], LSB-first. A [param count] of zero or less writes nothing.

method.name: reset
method.description: Discards everything written so far, so one writer can frame a second packet without a fresh allocation.

method.name: to_bytes
method.description: Flushes the partial final byte and returns the buffer.
